diagnostic:seed_stability.in_more_depth: Cross-fitting divides the data into folds at random, and the division is an arbitrary choice made by a random number generator. If the estimate changes materially when that choice changes, then the reported precision is describing sampling variation while ignoring a second source of variation that is just as real. The remedy when it fires is to average over several splits and to widen the interval accordingly, or to use a simpler learner that is less sensitive to which rows it trained on.

diagnostic:spec_curve.in_more_depth: Reporting three robustness checks is a sample of size three from a space the analyst chose. Running the grid -- covariate sets, calipers, bandwidths, trimming rules -- and drawing all of the answers puts the whole space on one picture, so a reader can see how much of it supports the conclusion. A finding that holds across most of the curve is stronger than one that holds for three hand-picked variants. A curve that crosses zero says the finding is a specification rather than a result. Where the marked specification sits in the ordering is itself worth reading.

diagnostic:strategy_paths.in_more_depth: The headline is a difference at the end of follow-up; the paths show how it got there. A gap that widens steadily is a plausible cumulative effect. A gap that is fully present in the first period, before the treatment could have acted, is a sign the models are picking up differences between the people following each strategy rather than the strategies themselves. Both paths come from the same fitted models, so the difference between them is exactly as good as those models are.

diagnostic:subgroups.in_more_depth: Each subgroup contrast is estimated the same way as the headline, so individually they are sound. The difficulty is collective: with twenty contrasts and no real differences at all, you expect one to cross the conventional threshold by luck, and it is that one that tends to get written up. The defence is to say in advance which subgroups you would examine, and to label everything else as exploration. Where a stricter threshold is appropriate, this panel reports what it would be for the number of contrasts actually run.

diagnostic:subset_stability.in_more_depth: Half the data gives a noisier estimate, and that is expected: the interval should widen by roughly the square root of two. What is not expected is draws that contradict each other, or a spread far wider than the loss of precision explains. That pattern means the estimate depends on which rows happened to be included, which is a different and worse problem than ordinary sampling noise. This is a blunt check and a useful one, because it needs no assumptions beyond the ones the analysis already makes.
diagnostic:subset_stability.one_liner: Refit the analysis on random parts of the data and see whether the answer stays put.
diagnostic:subset_stability.plain_language: Refit the analysis on random parts of the data and see whether the answer stays put.

diagnostic:temporal_ordering.in_more_depth: A variable cannot confound a choice that had already been made. If a measurement was taken after treatment started, adjusting for it does not remove bias; it removes part of the effect, because some of what the treatment did shows up in that measurement. In longitudinal data this is easy to get wrong, because the same variable appears at many time points and only some of them are eligible. The rule is simple to state and worth restating: a covariate may adjust a treatment decision only if it was recorded before that decision.
diagnostic:temporal_ordering.one_liner: A check that every variable used to adjust a decision was measured before that decision was taken.
diagnostic:temporal_ordering.plain_language: A check that every variable used to adjust a decision was measured before that decision was taken.

diagnostic:tmle_targeting.in_more_depth: Targeted learning starts from an outcome model's prediction and then applies one small correction designed to remove the bias that a prediction-focused model leaves behind. That correction is driven by the treatment probabilities, so its size tells you two things at once: how far off the initial outcome model was, and how extreme the weights are. A small, cleanly converged correction is the healthy case. A large one is not automatically wrong, but it means the answer is coming from the correction rather than from the model it corrected, and the overlap diagnostics are then the ones to read.

diagnostic:trim_cost.in_more_depth: Trimming discards units whose estimated chance of treatment is too extreme for a stable comparison. It is a defensible response to poor overlap, and it is not free: the units dropped are not a random sample, they are precisely the ones least like anybody in the other arm. After trimming, the estimate refers to the units that remain. If a fifth of the treated group has gone, "the effect of the programme on participants" is no longer what the number means, and the sample flow records the change so the report can say so.

diagnostic:trim_stability.in_more_depth: If the estimate barely moves as you trim more aggressively, the tails were not doing much and the finding is about the bulk of the data. If it walks steadily in one direction, the answer is being set by the units with the least comparable counterparts -- the ones the model had to extrapolate for. There is no threshold that is correct in general. The point of the curve is to make the choice visible rather than to make it for you, and to let a reader see whether the headline sits in the middle of the range or at one end of it.

diagnostic:unobserved_confounder.in_more_depth: Every adjustment in an observational design rests on having measured the things that pushed people towards treatment and also move the outcome. That assumption cannot be checked against the data, because the variables in question are precisely the ones you do not have. What can be done is to imagine one and see what it would need to look like. If a variable would have to be more strongly related to both the treatment and the outcome than anything you actually measured, the finding is fairly robust. If an ordinary, unremarkable variable would be enough, it is not. That comparison -- against the covariates you did collect -- is what makes the exercise informative rather than decorative.
diagnostic:unobserved_confounder.one_liner: Nobody can prove there is no missing common cause. This asks the answerable question instead: how strong would one have to be to overturn the finding?
diagnostic:unobserved_confounder.plain_language: Nobody can prove there is no missing common cause. This asks the answerable question instead: how strong would one have to be to overturn the finding?

diagnostic:weak_iv_set.in_more_depth: The usual two-stage least squares interval assumes the instrument is strong. When it is not, that interval is simply wrong -- too narrow, and centred in the wrong place. The Anderson-Rubin set makes no such assumption. An unbounded set is not a failure of the method: it is the correct statement that the data cannot pin the parameter down, and reporting a tidy interval instead would be the failure.
diagnostic:weak_iv_set.one_liner: A confidence set built by inverting a test that stays valid however weak the instrument is. It can be an interval, several intervals, or the whole line.
diagnostic:weak_iv_set.plain_language: A confidence set built by inverting a test that stays valid however weak the instrument is. It can be an interval, several intervals, or the whole line.

diagnostic:weighted_balance.in_more_depth: Weighting for time-varying treatment is meant to create a pseudo-population in which the treatment decision at each period is unrelated to everything measured up to that point. This table is the check on whether it did: every covariate at every period, compared between the person-periods where treatment was given and those where it was not, after the weights are applied. The check deliberately uses the raw rather than the stabilised weights, because it is the raw ones that define the pseudo-population balance is supposed to hold in. Residual imbalance means the treatment model has not removed the confounding it was there to remove -- which is a modelling failure, and separate from the untestable assumption that everything relevant was measured at all.
diagnostic:weighted_balance.one_liner: Whether, after weighting, the treated and untreated person-periods look alike on the variables the weights were built from.

diagnostic:weights_by_period.in_more_depth: Weighting for time-varying treatment multiplies one weight per period together, so the product grows more extreme the longer the follow-up. A history that was mildly unusual at each of eight time points can end up with an enormous cumulative weight, and the estimate then rests on a handful of people. Watching the effective sample fall period by period is the clearest early warning this design gives. The point estimate will not show it, and neither will the standard error, which assumes the weighting worked.

estimand:ATE.in_more_depth: The most natural quantity and often the hardest to identify. It requires the comparison to be credible for every kind of unit, including those who would never realistically be treated, so it leans hardest on overlap. Where the treated and untreated groups barely resemble each other, the ATE is estimated partly by extrapolation, and an effect on the overlap population may be the more honest target.

estimand:ATO.in_more_depth: Overlap weights put most weight where the probability of treatment is near a half -- the units for whom the comparison is best supported -- and almost none where treatment was nearly certain either way. The result has the smallest variance among weighted estimators and never has an exploding weight. The price is that the population is defined by the data rather than by policy. It is an excellent stability check and an awkward headline: "the effect among the people where comparison was possible" is honest, but it is not a group a minister can point at.

estimand:ATT.in_more_depth: Usually the policy-relevant number for an existing programme: it describes the people the programme actually reached. It also asks less of the data than the ATE, because you only need comparison units that resemble the treated, not the other way round. It is the default for matching and for difference-in-differences, and it is what the sample flow is quietly protecting: if matching drops a fifth of the treated units, the ATT is now for the four fifths that remained, and that is a different population.

estimand:CACE.in_more_depth: The LATE by another name, in the setting where the instrument is random assignment. It scales the intention-to-treat effect by the share of people whose behaviour the offer changed. Both numbers are correct and they answer different questions. If the policy you are evaluating can only make an offer, the ITT is the effect of the policy. The CACE is the effect of the treatment on the people who accept it, which is what a clinician wants to know.

estimand:CATE.in_more_depth: The most useful and most abused quantity in the catalogue. A flexible model will always produce varying predictions, including from noise, so the question is never "is there heterogeneity" but "is this ranking real". Two checks make it credible. Calibration asks whether the units predicted to benefit most actually did. The rank-weighted effect asks whether treating in the model's recommended order beats treating at random, and gives a standard error for the answer. Honest splitting -- choosing where the subgroups are on different rows from the ones that estimate their effects -- is what stops the estimate being optimistic by construction.

estimand:GATE.in_more_depth: Pre-specification is what separates a group effect from a fishing expedition. With a handful of groups defined in advance -- by age band, by region, by baseline severity -- the estimates are interpretable and the multiplicity correction is manageable. estimand:ITT.in_more_depth: It preserves the randomisation exactly, so it is the estimate that needs no extra assumptions. It is also diluted by noncompliance: an effective treatment with 30% take-up shows a small ITT, and that small number is the correct description of the policy as implemented. Reporting both the ITT and the complier effect, and saying which question each answers, is almost always better than choosing one.

estimand:LATE.in_more_depth: In an instrumental-variables design the compliers are the people the instrument moved -- and you cannot identify who they are, only their average effect. In a regression discontinuity the analogous group is units at the threshold. Different instruments move different people and therefore identify different numbers. Two studies with different instruments can both be right and still disagree, which is a feature of the estimand rather than a contradiction.

estimand:cohort_ATT.in_more_depth: The building block of modern difference-in-differences. Instead of one coefficient, you get a matrix: what the 2014 adopters experienced in 2015, in 2016, and so on. Everything else -- an overall effect, an event study, a per-cohort summary -- is an explicit average of these with weights you can see. That explicitness is the point. Two-way fixed effects also produces a weighted average, but with weights nobody chose and which can be negative.

estimand:dose_response.in_more_depth: A single linear coefficient assumes the tenth unit of a dose does what the first did, which is rarely true: effects saturate, and sometimes reverse. A dose-response curve estimates the whole function, with the positivity requirement now applying at every dose level -- and it usually fails at the extremes, where few units received that much.

tour.body: Four methods, not one. Matching, weighting, outcome regression and the doubly robust estimator disagree here, and the disagreement is the finding.

tour.body: There is no headline number when several methods ran. Outcome regression sits highest because it reaches furthest into the region where the two groups do not overlap at all. Propensity weighting sits far below zero, on the wrong side of no effect entirely, because it has almost nobody comparable to lean on. Matching, and the doubly robust method that fits both a model of who took part and a model of earnings so that either one being right is enough, land close to the built-in effect. The spread between the four is the finding, and it is a statement about this data rather than about the methods.

method:bounds.manski.title: Manski bounds

what_it_assumes.explains: Treated and untreated units are comparable once you condition on the confounders you measured. Everything that pushed people towards treatment and also moves the outcome is in your adjustment set.
what_it_assumes.title: Exchangeability / no unmeasured confounding
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Treatment was chosen by people who knew something about the likely outcome that you do not observe. Clinical judgement, self-selection into a programme, and administrative triage are the classic cases.

what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

what_it_assumes.explains: Assignment really was by chance, and nothing after assignment broke the comparison -- no differential dropout, no crossover you have not modelled.
what_it_assumes.title: Randomisation held
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Dropout differs across arms; take-up is far from assignment; the randomiser was a person with discretion.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument actually moves treatment, and moves it enough that the resulting estimate is not mostly noise.
what_it_assumes.title: Instrument relevance
what_it_assumes.worry_when: An effective F below about 10; a first-stage coefficient that is substantively tiny even if statistically significant; many instruments.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment. On the board, that is the arrow you did not draw.
what_it_assumes.title: Exclusion restriction
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is a policy that changed several things at once; it is correlated with geography, time or institutions that have their own effects; it was chosen because it predicted the outcome.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument pushes everyone the same way, or not at all. Nobody takes the treatment only because they were discouraged from it.
what_it_assumes.title: Monotonicity / no defiers
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is an incentive that could plausibly backfire for some people, or it is a judge or examiner whose leniency ordering differs across case types.

when_not_to_use: The bounds are often wide enough to include zero, which is informative and unpopular. Narrowing them means adding assumptions, and those should be stated.
when_to_use: The honest floor. When the point estimate rests on assumptions nobody can defend, an interval that rests on almost none is worth more than a number that rests on many.

what_it_assumes.explains: Without the policy, treated and comparison groups would have moved the same way. Not that they were at the same level -- that their paths would have been parallel.
what_it_assumes.title: Parallel trends
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.

what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_not_to_use: It leans harder on the additive unit-plus-period model than the 2x2 estimators do -- if untreated paths are not parallel, that shows up as effect rather than as a failed diagnostic. Pre-period effects are zero by construction unless periods are held out, so a test on a model that saw the pre-period is not a test.
when_to_use: It uses every untreated cell in the panel to build the counterfactual, which makes it the most efficient of the staggered estimators when the unit-and-period model is right. The logic is also the easiest to say out loud: what happened, minus what the untreated cells say would have.

options.help: Units that never adopt are the cleanest comparison. Units that have not adopted yet give you more of them, at the cost of assuming the late adopters were on the same path. If nobody stays untreated the estimator switches to not-yet-treated on its own and says so.

options.help: Doubly robust uses an outcome model and a comparison-group model together and is right if either is. IPW reweights the comparison group; Reg models the change in the outcome. With no covariates all three are the same plain difference of differences.

options.name: est_method

options.help: Simple weights every treated cohort-period by cohort size. Group averages each cohort's own effect. Dynamic averages the periods since adoption. Calendar averages the years. They answer different questions and all four are reported.
options.label: Headline average
options.name: aggregation

options.help: Universal compares every period with the one just before adoption, which is what the event-study picture usually means. Varying compares each pre-period with the period before it, which shows period-to-period drift instead of accumulated drift.
options.label: Measure each period against
options.name: base_period

options.help: A pointwise interval is right for one period and wrong for the picture: read five periods at once and one will fall outside by chance. This widens the band so the whole path is covered together.

options.name: cband

options.help: Multiplier-bootstrap draws for the simultaneous band. Seeded by the run seed, so the band is reproducible.

options.help: Bounds the weights when a unit is almost certain to be in the adopting cohort. Clipping is counted and reported, never silent.

when_not_to_use: The comparison group can be thin: with few never-treated units every cohort leans on the same handful of places, and the interval will not tell you that. when_not_to_use: Doubly robust is not doubly safe. When some units are almost certain to be adopters, the weights blow up and the outcome model quietly takes over by extrapolation. Adoption is staggered -- the doubly robust 2x2 still works cohort by cohort, but did.callaway_santanna is the same thing with the aggregations and the simultaneous bands.

when_not_to_use: This is arithmetic, not an estimator: the weights have no standard errors, and the headline number it decomposes is still the two-way fixed effects estimate with all of its problems. Simplifications named in the printout: balanced panel only, binary absorbing treatment, always-treated units dropped rather than used as an extra comparison group, and covariates ignored.
Every unit adopts on the same date -- then there is a single comparison and nothing to decompose.
when_to_use: It is the fastest way to see whether a staggered two-way fixed effects number is trustworthy. If most of the weight sits on later-versus-earlier-treated comparisons, the estimate is telling you about the weighting scheme rather than the policy.

when_not_to_use: Saturating cohort by relative period costs a lot of parameters, so with many cohorts and short panels the individual points get noisy. Without a never-treated group the last cohort becomes the comparison and its own effect is absorbed into the period effects, biasing everything else.
when_to_use: It is the event-study picture people already read, repaired. The saturated cohort-by-period terms make it impossible for one cohort to serve as another's control, which is the contamination that makes an ordinary event study misleading under staggered adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.

when_not_to_use: It buys robustness with a new assumption: the gap between the two groups inside a unit must have been on parallel paths. If the policy also affected the supposedly unaffected group -- spillovers, general equilibrium -- the third difference subtracts part of the effect. Under staggered adoption the same weighting critique as two-way fixed effects applies, and there is no Callaway-Sant'Anna style version here.
The third dimension does not vary inside a unit and period -- then it is effect heterogeneity across units, not a third difference.
when_to_use: When something else was happening in the treated units at the same time, the third difference sweeps it out: any shock that hit both groups inside a unit and period equally cancels. It rescues designs where plain parallel trends is not credible.

when_not_to_use: Under staggered adoption the coefficient is a variance-weighted average of every 2x2 comparison in the panel, including ones that use already-treated units as controls. When effects grow over time or differ across cohorts, that average is not the ATT and can even take the wrong sign. Run did.goodman_bacon to see the weights, and did.callaway_santanna or did.sun_abraham for the ATT.
Units adopt at more than one date (staggered adoption) and effects may grow over time or differ across cohorts -- then this number is a weighted average of comparisons, not an ATT.
when_to_use: It is the number most published papers report and most referees expect, so it belongs in the comparison. With a single adoption date and no covariates it is exactly the 2x2.

what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_not_to_use: With two periods parallel trends cannot be tested at all -- you are asserting that the comparison group's change is what the treated group's change would have been. Few clusters make the confidence interval optimistic. Covariates enter linearly and additively only; there are no covariate-by-period interactions.
when_to_use: When one group is treated at one date, this is the whole design and everyone can see the four numbers it is made of. Nothing is hidden inside a fixed-effects machine.

method:its.arima.title: ARIMA with an intervention

what_it_assumes.explains: Nothing else changed at the same moment that also moves the outcome.
what_it_assumes.title: No co-interventions at the interruption
what_it_assumes.worry_when: A busy policy period; a national event at the same date; a change in how the outcome was measured or coded at the same date.

what_it_assumes.explains: The line you fit before the interruption is the line the outcome would have continued to follow.
what_it_assumes.title: Functional form of the counterfactual trend
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Few pre-period points; residual autocorrelation that survives the model; the estimate flips when you add a seasonal term or a quadratic trend.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

when_not_to_use: The order is chosen by AIC, and near-ties are common; different orders can move the intervention coefficient. Nothing here tests causality: the coefficient is just the size of shift the model wants at that date. Standard errors are asymptotic and optimistic in short series. Simplifications, stated plainly: the search is a small two-stage AIC grid rather than full stepwise auto.arima, no seasonal unit-root test is run, and this is not CausalImpact - there is no Bayesian structural time series and no posterior.
Fewer than about 30 pre-interruption periods, where ARIMA orders are not identified
when_to_use: When the series has real memory - last month's value predicts this month's beyond any trend - segmented regression leaves that correlation in the residuals and only patches the standard errors. An ARIMA models it, and its pre-period forecast is an honest, widening counterfactual band.

what_it_assumes.explains: The line you fit before the interruption is the line the outcome would have continued to follow.
what_it_assumes.title: Functional form of the counterfactual trend
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Few pre-period points; residual autocorrelation that survives the model; the estimate flips when you add a seasonal term or a quadratic trend.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

when_not_to_use: It trades one assumption for another: instead of assuming the trend would have continued, you assume the two series would have moved in parallel. A control that was itself partly exposed pulls the estimate towards zero. Averaging controls that sit at very different levels lets the biggest one decide the answer. Simplification: the interacted model uses Driscoll-Kraay standard errors, which lean on having a reasonable number of periods and are thin on the cross-sectional side when there are only two or three series.
No untreated series measured on the same calendar exists
when_to_use: A single interrupted series cannot tell your intervention apart from anything else that happened that month. A control series that was not exposed can, and the control's own level and slope change are reported so you can see whether the shock was shared.

what_it_assumes.explains: The line you fit before the interruption is the line the outcome would have continued to follow.
what_it_assumes.title: Functional form of the counterfactual trend
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Few pre-period points; residual autocorrelation that survives the model; the estimate flips when you add a seasonal term or a quadratic trend.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

when_not_to_use: The counterfactual is a straight line projected forward, and nothing in the data tests it. Anything else that happened at the same date is inside the estimate. Autocorrelated residuals make plain intervals far too narrow, so HAC is the default and the Ljung-Box test is not optional. what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument actually moves treatment, and moves it enough that the resulting estimate is not mostly noise.
what_it_assumes.title: Instrument relevance
what_it_assumes.worry_when: An effective F below about 10; a first-stage coefficient that is substantively tiny even if statistically significant; many instruments.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment. On the board, that is the arrow you did not draw.
what_it_assumes.title: Exclusion restriction
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is a policy that changed several things at once; it is correlated with geography, time or institutions that have their own effects; it was chosen because it predicted the outcome.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument pushes everyone the same way, or not at all. Nobody takes the treatment only because they were discouraged from it.
what_it_assumes.title: Monotonicity / no defiers
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is an incentive that could plausibly backfire for some people, or it is a judge or examiner whose leniency ordering differs across case types.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_not_to_use: Exclusion is untestable and usually the weakest link: if the instrument reaches the outcome by any other route, the bias is the violation divided by the first stage, which is enormous when the instrument is weak. Two-stage least squares is also the estimator that degrades worst under weak instruments: it is biased towards ordinary least squares and its interval is too short.
The Olea-Pflueger effective first-stage F is below about 10; report the Anderson-Rubin set instead.
when_to_use: The standard instrumental-variables estimator, and the one every referee reads without translation. With a strong first stage it is efficient and its interval is honest.

when_not_to_use: Exclusion is untestable and usually the weakest link: if the instrument reaches the outcome by any other route, the bias is the violation divided by the first stage, which is enormous when the instrument is weak. The set can be unbounded or empty, which people read as a bug: unbounded means the data cannot rule out large effects, and empty means the instruments contradict each other.
when_to_use: Its coverage does not depend on the first stage being strong. When the instrument is weak this is the only interval on the screen that means what it says, and an unbounded set is a real answer, not a failure.

what_it_assumes.worry_when: Clinical measurements taken after the dose was changed; employment status recorded at the end of a period used to explain treatment at its start.

what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.explains: No unmeasured confounding of the treatment-outcome relationship, and none of the mediator-outcome relationship either, even after conditioning on treatment.
what_it_assumes.title: Sequential ignorability
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There is a variable affected by treatment that also confounds the mediator-outcome relationship. Under that structure the natural effects are not identified at all.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.

when_not_to_use: Requires a correctly specified blip function, and the estimating equations can have multiple roots.
when_to_use: More robust to positivity violations than weighting, because it does not divide by a treatment probability.

what_it_assumes.explains: Treated and untreated units are comparable once you condition on the confounders you measured. Everything that pushed people towards treatment and also moves the outcome is in your adjustment set.
what_it_assumes.title: Exchangeability / no unmeasured confounding
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Treatment was chosen by people who knew something about the likely outcome that you do not observe. Clinical judgement, self-selection into a programme, and administrative triage are the classic cases.

what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_not_to_use: Cross-world independence cannot be tested by any experiment, ever. And if anything the treatment caused also confounds the mediator-outcome relation, natural effects are not identified at all -- that is what interventional effects are for.
A mediator-outcome confounder that the treatment affects is on the board
when_to_use: It is the decomposition most readers have in mind, it adds up exactly, and it is the right answer when the mediator has no confounder that treatment itself caused.

when_not_to_use: A forest will always return a spread of effects, including when there is none. Read the calibration slope and the RATE before describing heterogeneity. when_to_use: The standard way to ask who benefits without fishing: honest sample splitting inside every tree, out-of-bag predictions, and a calibration test that tells you whether the ranking is real.

what_it_assumes.title: Exchangeability / no unmeasured confounding

what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.

when_not_to_use: Doubly robust is not doubly safe. When propensities approach 0 or 1 the weights explode, clipping kicks in, and the estimand quietly becomes something about a population you did not choose. The run reports how many units were clipped and at what threshold. Machine learning does not identify anything. Cross-fitting removes the bias that comes from fitting flexible models on the same rows you estimate with; it does nothing about a confounder you never measured.
Fewer than about 200 rows, where cross-fitting has too little to work with.
when_to_use: No restriction on how the effect varies, two chances to get the adjustment right, and a standard error from the score's own influence function. This is the default causal ML estimator for a binary treatment.

what_it_assumes.title: Exchangeability / no unmeasured confounding
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Treatment was chosen by people who knew something about the likely outcome that you do not observe. Clinical judgement, self-selection into a programme, and administrative triage are the classic cases.

what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_not_to_use: The S-learner can regularise the treatment effect away to nothing. The T-learner inherits both outcome models' biases. None of the per-unit effects carries an interval, and the plain average of a learner's predictions is shrunk, which is why it is never the headline here. Machine learning does not identify anything. Cross-fitting removes the bias that comes from fitting flexible models on the same rows you estimate with; it does nothing about a confounder you never measured.
You want one average effect and nothing else -- ml.dml_irm is the same score with less machinery.
when_to_use: Comparing meta-learners on the same folds is the cheapest way to see how much of your 'heterogeneity' is the learner rather than the world.

what_it_assumes.worry_when: Treatment was chosen by people who knew something about the likely outcome that you do not observe. Clinical judgement, self-selection into a programme, and administrative triage are the classic cases.

what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_not_to_use: Full matching can produce very unequal set sizes, so the effective sample size is the number to watch rather than the count of matched units.
when_to_use: Greedy nearest-neighbour matching depends on the order units are processed; optimal matching does not, and full matching keeps every unit by forming variable-ratio sets.

what_it_assumes.explains: Without the policy, treated and comparison groups would have moved the same way. Not that they were at the same level -- that their paths would have been parallel.
what_it_assumes.title: Parallel trends
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: At every period, the things that drive the treatment decision and also affect the outcome are measured -- and measured before that decision.
what_it_assumes.title: No unmeasured time-varying confounding
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Clinical measurements taken after the dose was changed; employment status recorded at the end of a period used to explain treatment at its start.

what_it_assumes.explains: No unmeasured confounding of the treatment-outcome relationship, and none of the mediator-outcome relationship either, even after conditioning on treatment.
what_it_assumes.title: Sequential ignorability
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There is a variable affected by treatment that also confounds the mediator-outcome relationship. Under that structure the natural effects are not identified at all.

when_not_to_use: The targeting step is driven by inverse propensity weights, so extreme propensities move the estimate a long way and the interval with it. The run reports how far the targeting moved the number and whether the score equation was actually solved. Machine learning does not identify anything. Cross-fitting removes the bias that comes from fitting flexible models on the same rows you estimate with; it does nothing about a confounder you never measured.
Overlap is so poor that most units sit at the propensity clip; then the fluctuation is fitting the boundary, not the data.
when_to_use: Doubly robust like AIPW, but the estimate is a prediction from a model, so it stays inside the bounds of the outcome -- a weighted estimator can return a risk difference no data could produce.

what_it_assumes.title: Randomisation held
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Dropout differs across arms; take-up is far from assignment; the randomiser was a person with discretion.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.

when_not_to_use: The CACE needs the exclusion restriction -- the offer must not affect the outcome except through take-up, which unblinded trials break routinely -- and monotonicity, which cannot be tested. It describes compliers, a group nobody can point at in the data, and it is not transportable to a place where different people would comply. The delta-method interval degrades as the first stage weakens; the bootstrap interval is reported alongside for that reason. No weak-instrument-robust (Anderson-Rubin) set is computed here.
Take-up moves by less than a few percentage points -- the ratio is then a small denominator away from meaningless; report the ITT.
when_to_use: Take-up was imperfect, so the difference between the arms measures the offer and not the programme. Reporting only one of the two numbers hides which question was answered.

what_it_assumes.explains: Assignment really was by chance, and nothing after assignment broke the comparison -- no differential dropout, no crossover you have not modelled.
what_it_assumes.title: Randomisation held
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Dropout differs across arms; take-up is far from assignment; the randomiser was a person with discretion.

when_not_to_use: Cluster-robust standard errors are justified by the number of clusters, not the number of rows: with fewer than about forty they are too small even with CR2. This adapter uses G - 1 degrees of freedom rather than the Bell-McCaffrey/Satterthwaite approximation, which can be optimistic when cluster sizes are unequal. If cluster size correlates with the effect, the individual-level and cluster-level answers differ and neither is wrong.
Fewer than about fifteen clusters -- prefer randomisation inference, which does not need a large-G approximation.
when_to_use: Assignment happened to whole groups, so outcomes inside a group are not independent draws. Treating rows as independent would make the interval far too narrow.

what_it_assumes.explains: Assignment really was by chance, and nothing after assignment broke the comparison -- no differential dropout, no crossover you have not modelled.
what_it_assumes.title: Randomisation held
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Dropout differs across arms; take-up is far from assignment; the randomiser was a person with discretion.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_not_to_use: It tests the sharp null that treatment changed nothing for anyone, which is not the null that the average effect is zero; rejecting it is a weaker statement than it looks. The permutation scheme must match how assignment was actually done -- miss the blocks or the clusters and the p-value is wrong in a way no amount of computation fixes. Small designs admit few distinct assignments, which puts a floor under the p-value. The interval, when produced, assumes a constant additive effect.
when_to_use: The randomisation is the only thing this p-value relies on. No normal approximation, no large-sample argument, no variance model -- which matters most exactly when the sample is small, the outcome is skewed, or there are few clusters.

what_it_assumes.explains: Assignment really was by chance, and nothing after assignment broke the comparison -- no differential dropout, no crossover you have not modelled.
what_it_assumes.title: Randomisation held
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Dropout differs across arms; take-up is far from assignment; the randomiser was a person with discretion.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_not_to_use: Block fixed effects silently report a precision-weighted average rather than the ATE when the treated share differs across blocks. Blocks with one unit in an arm give no within-block variance, so the standard error leans on a pooled approximation this adapter names in its printout. Blocks with only one arm are dropped, which narrows the population the estimate describes.
The blocks were not part of the randomisation -- blocking after the fact on a variable measured post-treatment is not stratification.
when_to_use: Randomisation was run inside blocks, so the comparison has to be made inside them too. Ignoring the blocks throws away precision; averaging them the wrong way changes the estimand.

when_not_to_use: It divides by the jump in take-up. A small first stage makes the interval explode and the point estimate meaningless, and the answer only describes the people the cutoff moved -- not everyone at the cutoff, and certainly not everyone. The bandwidth selector is named in the Classic tab and the variance is heteroskedasticity- or cluster-robust rather than rdrobust's nearest-neighbour estimator, so numbers will be close but need not match to the last digit.
The treatment jump at the cutoff is below about 0.1

when_not_to_use: Estimating a derivative is far noisier than estimating a level, so kink designs need much more data than they look like they need, and they are more sensitive to curvature in the underlying relationship. The number is a change in slope -- per unit of the running variable -- and must never be reported as an effect size. This is capy.py's own local-polynomial code, not rdrobust. The bandwidth selector is named in the Classic tab and the variance is heteroskedasticity- or cluster-robust rather than rdrobust's nearest-neighbour estimator, so numbers will be close but need not match to the last digit.
Fewer than a few thousand observations inside a plausible bandwidth
when_to_use: Benefit formulas, tax schedules and subsidy rules usually bend rather than switch. When that is the rule you have, the kink is the discontinuity, and reading it as a level jump would be wrong.

what_it_assumes.explains: The weighted combination of untreated units reproduces the treated unit's pre-period path closely enough to stand in for it afterwards.
what_it_assumes.title: Pre-treatment fit from the donor pool
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Visible pre-period gaps; a short pre-period relative to the number of donors; one donor carrying most of the weight.

what_it_assumes.explains: The treated unit's characteristics can be written as a weighted average of the donors', with weights that do not go negative.
what_it_assumes.title: Treated unit inside the donor convex hull
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treated unit is at an extreme of the donor distribution on the predictors, or the pre-period gap has a persistent level offset.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

when_not_to_use: If the donors cannot reproduce the treated unit before the intervention, the gap afterwards is fit error wearing a policy costume. Weights that pile onto one donor make this a two-unit comparison. With few donors the permutation test cannot produce a small p-value however large the effect, and a donor that had its own shock around the intervention contaminates the comparison. This implementation solves the weight problem with projected gradient plus SLSQP rather than Synth's own solvers, and its cross-validated V is a bounded search, not a global optimum.
when_to_use: For one treated unit and a run of pre-treatment periods this is the standard, and its output is legible to non-specialists: a line, a shadow line, and the distance between them. The weights are transparent, so a reader can argue with the comparison rather than with a coefficient.

what_it_assumes.explains: The weighted combination of untreated units reproduces the treated unit's pre-period path closely enough to stand in for it afterwards.
what_it_assumes.title: Pre-treatment fit from the donor pool
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Visible pre-period gaps; a short pre-period relative to the number of donors; one donor carrying most of the weight.

what_it_assumes.explains: The treated unit's characteristics can be written as a weighted average of the donors', with weights that do not go negative.
what_it_assumes.title: Treated unit inside the donor convex hull
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treated unit is at an extreme of the donor distribution on the predictors, or the pre-period gap has a persistent level offset.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

when_not_to_use: The correction can be larger than the original estimate, at which point the outcome model rather than the donor pool is doing the work. The augmented weights can be negative, which means extrapolating outside the donor pool. This implementation offers ridge ASCM only (no covariate or general outcome-model augmentation), picks the penalty by holding out late pre-treatment periods with the SC weights held fixed, and reports placebo inference rather than augsynth's jackknife+ intervals.
The plain synthetic control already fits the pre-treatment period well - then the correction is noise you do not need.
when_to_use: Poor pre-treatment fit is the usual reason a synthetic control fails, and augmentation is the honest response: it estimates the leftover bias and subtracts it, while reporting the uncorrected number beside it so you can see how much of the answer is the correction.

what_it_assumes.explains: The treated unit's characteristics can be written as a weighted average of the donors', with weights that do not go negative.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: Without the policy, treated and comparison groups would have moved the same way. Not that they were at the same level -- that their paths would have been parallel.
what_it_assumes.title: Parallel trends
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_not_to_use: There are no donor weights to inspect, so the comparison is much harder to argue with than a synthetic control's. The pre-treatment fit is in-sample and therefore flattering by construction - the placebo-in-time panel is the real check. This implementation uses soft-impute with additive unit and time effects and a single 20% hold-out for the penalty, and its placebo refits reuse that penalty, so the permutation test conditions on it.
Very short panels: with a handful of periods there is no low-rank structure to learn and the fit is mostly the fixed effects.
when_to_use: It does not need the treated unit to sit inside the donors' convex hull, it uses information from every cell of the panel rather than the treated unit's own history alone, and it handles interactive fixed effects that break parallel trends.

what_it_assumes.title: Randomisation held
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Dropout differs across arms; take-up is far from assignment; the randomiser was a person with discretion.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

what_it_assumes.explains: Treated and untreated units are comparable once you condition on the confounders you measured. Everything that pushed people towards treatment and also moves the outcome is in your adjustment set.
what_it_assumes.title: Exchangeability / no unmeasured confounding
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Treatment was chosen by people who knew something about the likely outcome that you do not observe. Clinical judgement, self-selection into a programme, and administrative triage are the classic cases.

what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.explains: Without the policy, treated and comparison groups would have moved the same way. Not that they were at the same level -- that their paths would have been parallel.
what_it_assumes.title: Parallel trends
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.explains: People could not precisely control which side of the cutoff they landed on.
what_it_assumes.title: No manipulation of the running variable
what_it_assumes.worry_when: A visible spike or gap in the density at the cutoff; covariates that jump; a cutoff that people knew about and had time to respond to.

what_it_assumes.explains: Everything else that affects the outcome changes smoothly through the cutoff, so the only thing that jumps is the treatment.
what_it_assumes.title: Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Several rules share the threshold; the running variable is coarse, so "at the cutoff" is really a wide band; the estimate depends heavily on the bandwidth.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument actually moves treatment, and moves it enough that the resulting estimate is not mostly noise.
what_it_assumes.title: Instrument relevance
what_it_assumes.worry_when: An effective F below about 10; a first-stage coefficient that is substantively tiny even if statistically significant; many instruments.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment. On the board, that is the arrow you did not draw.
what_it_assumes.title: Exclusion restriction
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is a policy that changed several things at once; it is correlated with geography, time or institutions that have their own effects; it was chosen because it predicted the outcome.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument pushes everyone the same way, or not at all. Nobody takes the treatment only because they were discouraged from it.
what_it_assumes.title: Monotonicity / no defiers
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is an incentive that could plausibly backfire for some people, or it is a judge or examiner whose leniency ordering differs across case types.

what_it_assumes.explains: The weighted combination of untreated units reproduces the treated unit's pre-period path closely enough to stand in for it afterwards.
what_it_assumes.title: Pre-treatment fit from the donor pool
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Visible pre-period gaps; a short pre-period relative to the number of donors; one donor carrying most of the weight.

what_it_assumes.explains: The treated unit's characteristics can be written as a weighted average of the donors', with weights that do not go negative.
what_it_assumes.title: Treated unit inside the donor convex hull
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treated unit is at an extreme of the donor distribution on the predictors, or the pre-period gap has a persistent level offset.

what_it_assumes.explains: Nothing else changed at the same moment that also moves the outcome.
what_it_assumes.title: No co-interventions at the interruption
what_it_assumes.worry_when: A busy policy period; a national event at the same date; a change in how the outcome was measured or coded at the same date.

what_it_assumes.explains: The line you fit before the interruption is the line the outcome would have continued to follow.
what_it_assumes.title: Functional form of the counterfactual trend
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Few pre-period points; residual autocorrelation that survives the model; the estimate flips when you add a seasonal term or a quadratic trend.

what_it_assumes.explains: No unmeasured confounding of the treatment-outcome relationship, and none of the mediator-outcome relationship either, even after conditioning on treatment.
what_it_assumes.title: Sequential ignorability
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There is a variable affected by treatment that also confounds the mediator-outcome relationship. Under that structure the natural effects are not identified at all.

what_it_assumes.explains: At every period, the things that drive the treatment decision and also affect the outcome are measured -- and measured before that decision.
what_it_assumes.title: No unmeasured time-varying confounding
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Clinical measurements taken after the dose was changed; employment status recorded at the end of a period used to explain treatment at its start.

when_not_to_use: The confounder is simulated. The grid says how strong one would have to be, never whether one exists, and the answer depends on the shape assumed for it.
when_to_use: Exchangeability cannot be tested, so the honest question is how much unmeasured confounding it would take. This answers it in units a reader can compare against the confounders you did measure.

what_it_assumes.explains: Treated and untreated units are comparable once you condition on the confounders you measured. Everything that pushed people towards treatment and also moves the outcome is in your adjustment set.
what_it_assumes.title: Exchangeability / no unmeasured confounding
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Treatment was chosen by people who knew something about the likely outcome that you do not observe. Clinical judgement, self-selection into a programme, and administrative triage are the classic cases.

what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

what_it_assumes.explains: At every period, the things that drive the treatment decision and also affect the outcome are measured -- and measured before that decision.
what_it_assumes.title: No unmeasured time-varying confounding
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Clinical measurements taken after the dose was changed; employment status recorded at the end of a period used to explain treatment at its start.

what_it_assumes.explains: No unmeasured confounding of the treatment-outcome relationship, and none of the mediator-outcome relationship either, even after conditioning on treatment.
what_it_assumes.title: Sequential ignorability
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There is a variable affected by treatment that also confounds the mediator-outcome relationship. Under that structure the natural effects are not identified at all.

what_it_assumes.explains: People could not precisely control which side of the cutoff they landed on.
what_it_assumes.title: No manipulation of the running variable
what_it_assumes.worry_when: A visible spike or gap in the density at the cutoff; covariates that jump; a cutoff that people knew about and had time to respond to.

what_it_assumes.explains: Everything else that affects the outcome changes smoothly through the cutoff, so the only thing that jumps is the treatment.
what_it_assumes.title: Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Several rules share the threshold; the running variable is coarse, so "at the cutoff" is really a wide band; the estimate depends heavily on the bandwidth.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument actually moves treatment, and moves it enough that the resulting estimate is not mostly noise.
what_it_assumes.title: Instrument relevance
what_it_assumes.worry_when: An effective F below about 10; a first-stage coefficient that is substantively tiny even if statistically significant; many instruments.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment. On the board, that is the arrow you did not draw.
what_it_assumes.title: Exclusion restriction
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is a policy that changed several things at once; it is correlated with geography, time or institutions that have their own effects; it was chosen because it predicted the outcome.

what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument pushes everyone the same way, or not at all. Nobody takes the treatment only because they were discouraged from it.
what_it_assumes.title: Monotonicity / no defiers
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is an incentive that could plausibly backfire for some people, or it is a judge or examiner whose leniency ordering differs across case types.

what_it_assumes.explains: The weighted combination of untreated units reproduces the treated unit's pre-period path closely enough to stand in for it afterwards.
what_it_assumes.title: Pre-treatment fit from the donor pool
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Visible pre-period gaps; a short pre-period relative to the number of donors; one donor carrying most of the weight.

what_it_assumes.explains: The treated unit's characteristics can be written as a weighted average of the donors', with weights that do not go negative.
what_it_assumes.title: Treated unit inside the donor convex hull
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treated unit is at an extreme of the donor distribution on the predictors, or the pre-period gap has a persistent level offset.

what_it_assumes.explains: Nothing else changed at the same moment that also moves the outcome.
what_it_assumes.title: No co-interventions at the interruption
what_it_assumes.worry_when: A busy policy period; a national event at the same date; a change in how the outcome was measured or coded at the same date.

what_it_assumes.explains: The line you fit before the interruption is the line the outcome would have continued to follow.
what_it_assumes.title: Functional form of the counterfactual trend
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Few pre-period points; residual autocorrelation that survives the model; the estimate flips when you add a seasonal term or a quadratic trend.

Individually randomised data with no clustering, where each group is one row
when_to_use: Panel and synthetic-control results are often one unit's story. This is the check that finds out, and it reads as a forest anyone can follow.
